query: Consider the following context: The recent trend of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) was studied extensively for their promising mechanical properties, but individual constituents' effects have remained unexplored. In that context, which method can be used for the effects of changing the percentage of elements of HfNbTaTiZr-HEA on the mechanical properties, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Varying the relative concentration of one principal element (e.g., increasing Hf at the expense of Ti) in HfNbTaTiZr HEAs synthesized by powder metallurgy (using spark plasma sintering) will alter the microstructure (grain refinement and secondary phase formation), which in turn will systematically increase hardness and yield strength while reducing ductility at room temperature.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr HEA produced via powder metallurgy by spark plasma sintering
generation.intervention: Systematically increase the percentage of Hf (reducing Ti proportionally) in the HfNbTaTiZr alloy
generation.conditions: Samples are processed under the same sintering (SPS) conditions and tested at room temperature
generation.structural_mediator: Microstructural changes including refined grain size and the potential formation of secondary phases or solid solution strengthening effects
generation.mechanism: Elemental variation modifies the local bonding environment and phase stability; increased Hf can enhance solid solution strengthening and promote microstructural refinement or secondary phase nucleation, increasing hardness and yield strength while limiting ductility.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in hardness and yield strength (approximately in the 10–20% range, acknowledging uncertainty in the exact magnitude) and a concurrent decrease in plasticity compared to the baseline equiatomic alloy.
generation.baseline: The standard equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr HEA with uniform elemental proportions prepared via SPS
generation.boundary: These effects are predicted for room temperature mechanical properties; the hypothesis does not extend to high-temperature behavior or long-term stability.
generation.uncertainty: Precise quantitative changes in mechanical properties are uncertain without experimental calibration, and the extent to which Hf dominates the observed effects over other elements needs verification.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare several series of HfNbTaTiZr HEA samples in which the Hf content is gradually increased (in 5 atomic % increments) while reducing Ti content accordingly, keeping the other elements constant. Process all samples using the same SPS protocol to ensure comparable densification. Perform mechanical tests (Vickers hardness, compression and/or tensile tests) and microstructural characterizations (SEM/TEM, XRD) at room temperature.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the observed mechanical properties do not show a consistent trend of increased hardness and yield strength (with a loss of ductility) concomitant with the predicted microstructural changes, or if changing Hf content produces no statistically significant differences compared to the baseline equiatomic composition, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract High entropy alloys (HEA) have been one of the most attractive groups of materials for researchers in the last several years. Since HEAs are potential candidates for many (e.g., refractory, cryogenic, medical) applications, their properties are studied intensively. The most frequent method of HEA synthesis is arc or induction melting. Powder metallurgy is a perspective technique of alloy synthesis and therefore in this work the possibilities of synthesis of HfNbTaTiZr HEA from powders were studied. Blended elemental powders were sintered, hot isostatically pressed, and subsequently swaged using a special technique of swaging where the sample is enveloped by a titanium alloy. This method does not result in a full density alloy due to cracking during swaging. Spark plasma sintering (SPS) of mechanically alloyed powders resulted in a fully dense but brittle specimen. The most promising result was obtained by SPS treatment of gas atomized powder with low oxygen content. The microstructure of HfNbTaTiZr specimen prepared this way can be refined by high pressure torsion deformation resulting in a high hardness of 410 HV10 and very fine microstructure with grain size well below 5
